# Hermes contract

Hermes is a hosted agent (hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) that lives outside
this repo. This is the contract it builds against — a reference, not a
tutorial. The Worker URL and the `X-Auth-Token` value live in Hermes's own
credential store and must never be committed here.

**The route list is `ROUTES` in `worker/worker.js`** (committed as `worker/routes.json`, regenerated by
`node tools/routes_build.mjs`). `tools/worker_test.mjs` probes the real Worker against it, so every route below exists
and every route the Worker answers is listed. Tables here mirror that list; if they disagree, `routes.json` wins.

Every request carries `X-Auth-Token: <token>`. KV is eventually consistent
(~60s) — Hermes must not read back a write to confirm it landed.

## Writing as Hermes: `X-Actor`, `X-Reason`, dry run, undo

Hermes and the app share `AUTH_TOKEN`, so a write is only logged to the Assistant activity list when Hermes says so:

- Send `X-Actor: hermes` and `X-Reason: <one line, why>` on every Hermes write. The write is then logged `who: "hermes"` and can be undone. Without `X-Actor` it is treated as the app and logs nothing. Any other `X-Actor` value is ignored; on the assistant token the header means nothing (that token always logs `"assistant"`).
- `?dryRun=1` on a write whose row says `dryRun` returns `{ changes, summary }` and writes nothing, logs nothing. A key without logging support answers `400 "dryRun not supported for this key"`.
- `GET /activity` → `{ entries: [{ id, at, who, key, why, summary, changes, undoes? }] }`, newest first, capped at 200.
- `POST /activity/undo { id }` restores the entry's items: `404` unknown entry, `409 {"error":"already undone"}`, `409 {"error":"changed since", changed}` when someone edited those items since. `force` ("Undo anyway") is the app's call and is ignored whenever `X-Actor` is set. An undo is itself logged.
- A write that fails validation logs nothing.

Not logged (`log: "unlogged"` in `routes.json`, each with a `why`): the app-owned mirrors `/plan`, `/prefs`, `/eaten-log`, `/planPrefs`, `/cooks`; `/settings` (profile data); `/drafts` and `PUT /meal/:id/rating` (inert/informational).

## Routes

`A` = the assistant token may call it too. Everything else is Hermes-only (assistant gets `403`). Any other method on a path answers `405`.

### Read-only

| Call | A | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /library` `/plan` `/prefs` `/eaten-log` `/planFlag` `/planPrefs` `/cooks` | library, plan, prefs, eaten-log | Raw KV mirrors; `null` when never written. `/plan`, `/prefs`, `/eaten-log`, `/planPrefs`, `/cooks` are app-owned (Hermes `PUT`s to them are the app's job, not Hermes's). |
| `GET /discover?q=` | A | See below. |
| `GET /shopping` | A | The planned two-week list, see below. |
| `GET /shopping/lines` | A | The shared list lines (`{ updatedAt, lines }`); `/adhoc` is a view of it. |
| `GET /nutrition?date=` or `?from=&to=` | A | Approximate protein/coverage and gaps for a day (or a window; `gym=1` only with `date`). `400` if both `date` and `from`/`to`. |
| `GET /ranking?day=&slot=&n=` |  | The generator's top meals for a slot (`day` 1-14, `slot` default dinner, `n` 1-10 default 3). |
| `GET /why?meal=&day=&slot=` | A | `{ mealId, rank, reasons, approximate: true }`: why a meal sits where it does. `404 unknown meal`. |
| `GET /day?date=&gym=` | A | The Today screen as an ordered card list. `date` `YYYY-MM-DD` (default today, London), `gym` 0 or 1. |
| `GET /scale?meal=&portions=` | A | `{ mealId, portions, servings, lines, …shortfall, cookTime, storage }`; `portions` an integer 1-12. |
| `GET /cookable?n=` `/leftovers` `/quick?n=` `/expiring?days=` | A | Pantry- and cook-derived suggestions, see the table of shapes below. |
| `GET /substitutions` | A | `substitution-groups.json` verbatim. |
| `GET /product-ranking` | A | Products by £ per 25 g protein. |
| `GET /ratings` | A | `{ meals: { <mealId>: { rating?, note?, never?, at } } }`. |
| `GET /meal/:id/method` | A | `{ mealId, name, status: none\|drafted\|accepted, steps, ingredients }`; `404 unknown meal`. |
| `GET /drafts` | A | Meal drafts awaiting the app's accept: `{ updatedAt, drafts }`. |
| `GET /settings` | A | Profile settings (`{}` until written). |
| `GET /activity` | A | See above. |
| `GET /planDraft` | A | The parked plan draft (`null` when none). |
| `POST /plan/draft` | A | Read-like: `{ days?, keep?, avoid?, budget? }` → `{ draft, plan }` computed by the generator; stores nothing. `409` until the library is synced; `400` on a bad field. Fills around locked slots (the mirror may carry `locked: true`), eaten and `keep` slots. |

### Writes

| Call | A | Dry run | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PUT /library` | A | yes | Hermes may rewrite; the assistant is append-only (`403` otherwise). See below. |
| `PUT /pantry` | A | yes | Whole-array relay, see below. |
| `PUT /adhoc` | A | yes | The "ran out / want to buy" list; compatibility view over `shopping`. |
| `POST /shopping/lines { lines }` | A |  | Per-line last-write-wins merge into the shared list. |
| `PUT /planFlag` | A | yes | `{ requestedAt, ackedAt }`: "generate a new plan" banner. |
| `PUT /placements` | A | yes | A request queue, see below. |
| `PUT /dayHints` | A | yes | `{ updatedAt, days: { "YYYY-MM-DD": { effort: busy\|normal\|free, why? (≤80 chars) } } }`, at most 28 dates. Assistant-written; the app only reads it. |
| `PUT /today` | A | yes | `{ date, water, caffeine, gym, routineDone }` counters for one day. |
| `PUT /products` | A | yes | Product reference records, see below. |
| `PUT /meal-method { mealId, method }` | A | yes | Sets `method` and `methodStatus: "drafted"`, nothing else, never over an accepted one (`409`). Steps: 1-30 of `{ text ≤300, minutes? 1-600 }`. |
| `PUT /meal/:id/rating` | A |  | Merge any of `{ rating, note, never }`; server stamps `at`. `404 unknown meal`. |
| `POST /drafts` | A |  | A meal draft; ingredients are matched to known keys, hard exclusions run (`422` on a hit, `409` too many). `201 { id, unmatched }`. |
| `DELETE /drafts/:id` | A |  | `204`; `404 unknown draft`. |
| `POST /plan/apply { draft }` | A |  | Parks a draft from `/plan/draft` in `planDraft` for the app to adopt; never touches the plan. `409` until the library is synced. |
| `POST /plan/reflow { skipped?, eatingOut?, ranOut? }` | A |  | Re-plans only skipped / eating-out / ran-out slots (a skipped batch cook frees its leftover chain; eaten, locked and past slots stay) and parks the result as a pending `planDraft` (`reflow: true`). `409` without a synced library or plan; `400` on a bad day/slot/ranOut. Never writes the pantry. |
| `POST /activity/undo { id }` | A |  | See above. |
| `PUT /settings` | A |  | Written only here; validated (`400` with the reason), unknown keys come back in `ignored`. |
| `PUT /planDraft` |  | yes | Raw key write; prefer `POST /plan/apply`. |
| `PUT /plan` `/prefs` `/eaten-log` `/planPrefs` `/cooks` |  |  | App-owned mirrors; Hermes does not write them. |

### Queues (proposed by Hermes or the assistant, applied by the app)

| Call | A | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`/`PUT /placements` | A | See below. |
| `GET`/`PUT /eat-requests` | A | "I ate X" queue, see below. |

### Shapes that predate this list

| Capability | HTTP call | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Discover a meal | `GET /discover?q=<user's words>` | Returns meals already shaped for `mp_library` — append one to `meals` and `PUT /library` with no field translation. Read `substituted` aloud when non-empty (e.g. "swapped mushrooms for courgette"). `rejected` names anything skipped and why. |
| Answer nutrition/recipe Q&A | `GET /library` + the public `ingredient-nutrient-tags.json` / `nutrition-targets.json` | Approximate-coverage framing only, never precise calorie math. |
| Edit ingredients in a meal | `GET /library` → modify → `PUT /library` | Send the full `meals` array back and set `updatedAt` to now. A `400` means the body was malformed — re-read and retry with a corrected one. |
| "Generate a new plan" | `PUT /planFlag {"requestedAt": "<now ISO>", "ackedAt": null}` | The app shows a banner and generates on tap. Hermes replies "ready in the app" — it never renders a plan as chat text. |
| Track what food is on hand | `GET`/`PUT /pantry` | Body `{ updatedAt, items: [{ name, qty?, useBy?, storage? }] }` (`storage` = fridge\|freezer\|cupboard, else 400; `useBy` = `YYYY-MM-DD`, else 400; dropping it on a write clears it). No duplicate names (case-insensitive). Always fetch-then-write the full array. |
| Items due soon | `GET /expiring?days=N` | 0-30, default 2; `?today=` ISO; overdue included; `basis` entered\|estimate. |
| Pantry audit | `GET /pantry/audit?location=fridge\|freezer\|cupboard&limit=` `GET /pantry/sanity` `POST /pantry/audit {confirmed?, snooze?}` | Next batch to check (never-confirmed first; `unsorted` = items with no known location); sanity findings `negative-qty`, `implausible-qty`, `stale`, `no-use-by`, `duplicate`, minus snoozed ones. POST writes only `pantryAudit` (names must be in the pantry, snooze `days` 0-90, 0 clears), never `pantry`. `?today=` ISO. |
| What can I cook now? | `GET /cookable?n=` | `{ today, ready, nearMiss }` (n 1-20, default 10). Ready = nothing missing, near-miss = 1-2 missing; each pick `{ id, name, prepEffort, proteinGramsApprox, missing, urgency }`. |
| Leftovers | `GET /leftovers` | `{ today, leftovers: [{ id, mealId, name, portionsLeft, storage, eatBy, basis: "estimate", daysLeft, lastDay }] }`, soonest eat-by first. Mirrored from the app's `PUT /cooks`. |
| Night off cooking | `GET /quick?n=` | `{ today, items }` (n 1-20, default 5). Suggestions only; nothing is cooked or deducted. |
| Add to / clear "ran out / want to buy" | `GET`/`PUT /adhoc` | Same shape as `/pantry`. Use for "add X to my shopping list" — never `/pantry`. |
| Read a shopping screenshot into pantry quantities | `GET /pantry` → merge → `PUT /pantry` | Set each matching item's `qty` to `{ value, unit, raw }`; never a source of price, pack size or purchase date. |
| What's on the plan | `GET /plan` | Read-only, `mealId`+`eatenAt` per slot. Stale by construction; inform a placement with it, never trust it. |
| Taste counters | `GET /prefs` | Read-only counters per meal; softer framing, not a filter. |
| Variety over time | `GET /eaten-log` | Tags are frozen at eat time. |

Hermes writes to the raw PUTs above (`/planFlag`, `/library`, `/pantry`, `/adhoc`, `/placements`, `/dayHints`, `/products`, …) exactly as the app does, but with `X-Actor: hermes` and `X-Reason` so they appear in the activity list with Undo.

## `GET /discover`

- `q` present → `search.php?s=<q>` on TheMealDB; `q` blank/absent → one
  random meal via `random.php`.
- `200` body: `{ query, meals: [...], rejected: [...] }`, both arrays capped
  at 8. Each meal already passes the app's dietary exclusions (no mushroom,
  no standalone egg, no veg-in-toastie) — a mushroom recipe is either
  substituted (courgette) or dropped into `rejected`, never returned as-is.
- `502` on any TheMealDB failure (never a partial list, never a 500).

## `PUT /library`

Shape-validated only: `meals` must be an array, each meal needs a non-empty
`id`/`name` and an `ingredients` array, no duplicate ids. `meals: []` is
legal. No dietary rules are enforced on the way in — those apply only at
`/discover`, since a rule tweak here would risk locking the user out of
saving their own existing library.

A meal may optionally carry `variants: [{ id, name, ingredients, instructions?,
servings?, prepEffort? }]` — a linked variation of the same recipe (a
different sauce or side), not a separate meal. `id` is unique only within
that meal's own `variants` array; the meal's own top-level fields are the
default variant. If present, `variants` must be an array of objects each with
a non-empty `id`/`name` and an `ingredients` array, no duplicate variant ids
within the meal — same all-or-nothing rejection as the rest of this endpoint.
A family of variants is still one `meal.id`, so it counts as one meal
everywhere else (Discover dedupe, the variety guard).

## `GET /pantry` / `PUT /pantry`

Generic two-key relay, same as `/library`. Body shape: `{ updatedAt, items:
[{ name, qty? }] }`. `items` must be an array; each item needs a non-empty
`name` string; no duplicate names (case-insensitive, trimmed). `qty` is
either a free-text string (e.g. `"2"`, `"half a bag"`) or a structured
`{ value, unit, raw }` object — when structured, all three fields are
required: `value` a finite non-negative number, `unit` and `raw` non-empty
strings. `raw` is what the screenshot (or person) literally said; `unit` is
not enum-checked, but prefer `g`/`ml`/`each` where the source allows.
`items: []` is legal (empty pantry). Hermes should fetch-then-write — never
PUT from stale/cached data, since this clobbers the whole array.

As of Phase 31, the **app itself** also writes structured `qty` values here —
a cook deduction leaves a structured remainder, and a shortfall from a cook
lands on `/adhoc` as a structured `qty` too. So a `qty` Hermes reads back
isn't necessarily free text just because no person typed it; treat both
forms as equally possible on every read, regardless of who wrote them.

## `GET /products` / `PUT /products`

Product reference records (Phase 33a), whole-key like `/pantry`, both tokens. Body: `{ updatedAt, products: Product[] }`
(max 2000). `Product` = `{ id, barcode|null, name, brand?, ingredient?, per: "100g"|"100ml", servingSize?, pack?: {value, unit},
price? (GBP per pack), state?: raw|cooked|dry, nutrients: { <key>: { value >= 0, basis } }, source: scan|photo|manual, updatedAt }`.
`basis` is `label|off|cofid|usda|estimate` (precedence in that order; never overwrite a higher basis with a lower one).
Nutrient keys are `/^[a-z0-9_]+$/`: `energy_kcal`, `protein_g`, `carbohydrate_g`, `fat_g`, `saturates_g`, `sugars_g`, `fibre_g`,
`salt_g` plus micros. An absent key means unknown, never 0. `barcode` needs a valid GS1 check digit and `id === barcode`;
otherwise use `id: "p-<anything unique>"`. `ingredient` is a planner ingredient key (snake_case) and links the record to the
pantry item of that name. Fetch-then-write and merge per record by `updatedAt`: PUT replaces the whole list. Reference only:
the planner never reads it for ranking. 400 on a bad check digit, duplicate id, non-numeric value or unknown basis.

`GET /product-ranking` (both tokens, read-only; 405 otherwise) returns `{ ranked: [{ id, name, brand, per25g, estimated }] }`: products by £ per 25 g protein, cheapest first. Needs a g/kg pack and protein; price falls back to `pack-sizes.json` (`estimated: true`); ml products are left out. Informational only.

## `GET /adhoc` / `PUT /adhoc`

Identical body shape and validation to `/pantry` (including the string-or-
structured `qty`) — same relay, different KV key. This is the "ran out of /
want to buy this week" scratch list, separate from the planned two-week shop
that `buildLists` produces locally: the app's eat flow drops shortfalls
here, and a person can add to it by hand. Fetch-then-write applies the same
as `/pantry`. The planned list can be read through `GET /shopping` (below)
but never edited — it is derived from the plan.

## `GET /eaten-log` / `PUT /eaten-log`

Client-owned, write-only-from-the-app history mirror — same whole-array
replace pattern as `/pantry`, but the body is a **bare JSON array**, not an
`{updatedAt, ...}` object, because nothing acks or merges this key. Each
entry: `{ id, mealId, name, eatenAt, tags }`, where `id` is
`` `${mealId}:${eatenAt}` `` (dedup key), `eatenAt` is an ISO 8601 string
(not date-parsed by the Worker), and `tags` is an array of nutrient names
(may be `[]`). Capped at 200 entries, oldest dropped first. Unknown extra
keys on an entry are rejected, same as `/library`'s meal shape.

**Tags are frozen at eat time** — they're the nutrient names `tagsForMeal`
resolved against `ingredient-nutrient-tags.json` on the day the meal was
eaten. Re-tagging an ingredient later does not retroactively rewrite past
entries; don't assume an entry's `tags` reflect current tagging data.

The app never reads this key back — it's write-only from the app's side.
Hermes is the only reader, for questions about variety *over time* (as
opposed to `/plan`'s current-fortnight snapshot or `/prefs`' taste counters).

## `GET /plan`

Read-only mirror of the current 2-week plan, pushed by the app whenever it
saves (generate, swap, move, or eat). Body: `{ updatedAt, startDate, days:
[{ day, slots: { breakfast?/lunch?/dinner?/snack?: { mealId, eatenAt,
variantId? } } }] }` — empty slots are omitted, `variantId` is present only
when the slot has one (never `null`), and there is no name/description/
ingredient data in this key at all; join `mealId` (and `variantId`, if
present) against `/library` for that. This mirror
can lag the real plan by an arbitrary amount (it's a best-effort push, not
read-after-write) — use it only to *inform* a proposed placement, never to
decide one is safe. The app is the sole authority: every `PUT /placements`
entry is re-checked against the live local plan before it's applied.

## `PUT /placements`

A request queue, not a direct write — Hermes proposes, the app applies (or
rejects) on its own next load/resume. Body: `{ placements: [{ id, day
(1-14), slot ("breakfast"|"lunch"|"dinner"|"snack"), mealId, mealName,
variantId?, requestedAt }] }`. **Replace the whole array on every PUT** —
there is no append semantics server-side, and the app tracks its own ack
watermark by `requestedAt` so replays and reorders are harmless. A placement
is rejected, never silently dropped, when:

- the target slot already has `eatenAt` set — never overwrites eaten
  history, or
- `mealId` isn't in the person's local library.

`variantId` is optional; if given but not one of that meal's variant ids, the
placement still applies — just against the base recipe rather than bouncing
the whole placement.

Rejections surface in a dismissible banner in the app; there is no bridge
endpoint to read them back, so avoid re-proposing a placement Hermes has
reason to expect will bounce (e.g. a day it already saw as eaten via
`GET /plan`).

## `GET /prefs`

Read-only. Body: `{ updatedAt, prefs: { <mealId>: { name, liked, dismissed,
eaten, lastAt } } }` — three integer counters and a timestamp per meal, no
history log. There is no `PUT /prefs` for Hermes: counters are app-owned,
bumped only by the person's own like/save/dismiss/eat actions.

## `GET /shopping`

Read-only. Body: `{ updatedAt, startDate, lists: { "1": {...}, "8": {...} },
adhoc: [{ name, qty? }] }`. Each list is exactly what the shopping page's
`MP.ShoppingList.buildLists` returns — `{ shopDay, lines, staples, estimated,
total }`, each line `{ key, label, needed, packSize, unit, packs, price,
lineCost, estimated, meals, pantryQty?, onHand? }` — computed over the `/plan`
mirror, `/library` and `/pantry`, so it is **as stale as the plan mirror**
(`updatedAt` is the plan push time). `409` until library and plan have both
been synced.

## `GET /eat-requests` / `PUT /eat-requests`

The personal assistant's "I ate X" queue — same pattern as `/placements`:
the assistant proposes, the app applies (or rejects) on its next plan-page
load/resume. Body: `{ requests: [{ id, mealId, eatenAt, requestedAt }] }`,
whole-array replace, at most 50, no extra keys, `id` must be
`` `${mealId}:${eatenAt}` `` (the eaten-log id the app will write, so the
assistant can match it), dates must parse. The app acks by `requestedAt`
locally. A request lands on the first un-eaten slot holding that meal on the
plan day of `eatenAt`; it is rejected (banner) when there is none, never
forced, and goes through the normal eat flow (cook, or a portion of an open
cook) keeping `eatenAt`.

## Credentials

Two tokens, one per consumer: Hermes's `AUTH_TOKEN` (every route), and the personal assistant's `ASSISTANT_TOKEN`, which
reaches only the rows marked `A` above (`assistant: true` in `routes.json`; `ASSISTANT_ALLOWED` in the Worker). Its
`PUT /library` is **append only** (a body that changes an existing meal, or drops one the assistant didn't add itself,
is `403`), and `force` on undo is ignored. `403` elsewhere (e.g. `PUT /prefs`, `PUT /plan`). Never commit either token.

## Planning chat

`/chat` is a short-lived relay between the app's "Plan with Hermes" screen and Hermes. The thread lives in the `ChatRoom` Durable Object (not KV: a ~1 s poll can't live with KV's cache). Hermes token only; the assistant token gets 403. `tools/hermes_chat_bridge.py` runs on the PC, polls `GET /chat`, calls `hermes -z` once per user message and posts the reply.

- `POST /chat` `{ session, open: true, context }` resets the thread; `{ session, text, day, context }` appends a user message; `{ session, close: true }` ends it. `GET /chat?session=&since=` returns newer messages. `POST /chat/reply` `{ session, replyTo, text, edits, ask }` (needs `X-Actor: hermes`, else 403) posts Hermes's reply.
- Reply shape: `{ text, edits, ask }`. Edit types are a fixed set: `busy`, `free`, `noCook`, `chip`, `budget`, `lock`, `unlock`, `reroll`. **Hermes returns constraints and edits, never meals**; the app's generator picks the meals. `MP.PlanChat.validateReply` (Worker and app) drops anything else and `/chat/reply` answers `{ id, dropped }`; the bridge re-asks once when `dropped > 0`.
- To ask rather than guess, reply with `ask: true` and no edits.
- Max 40 messages per thread, 300 characters per user message. Stale session gets 409.

`context.cards` (on `POST /chat`) lists the tie or trade-off cards currently on screen in the app (e.g. `tie Tue: Chicken curry or Chilli`). The app wrote them; Hermes must not pick between them or contradict them.
